title: A single sub that fails alignment aborts the entire Stack & Share run and deletes the partial result, even though the code counts 'rejected' frames as a normal outcome
what_happened: With 'Apply calibration' off the stacker initialised on audit_L_024.fits with 34 stars, then the very first follower frame (audit_L_018.fits) was rejected for alignment residual and the whole run died: the dialog showed 'Stack & Share failed', no stacked_results row was written, and the log shows 'Live stacker stopped and resources released' one millisecond after the rejection -- frames 019-024 were never attempted. The native layer treats this as a per-frame rejection (it increments stats.rejected_alignment_failures and returns Err), and the Dart loop even has a framesRejected counter for exactly this case, but the counter is dead code: _addStackFrame is awaited without a try/catch, so the Err becomes an exception that escapes the for-loop into the run-level catch, which deletes the incomplete stacked_results row and rethrows.
expected: A frame that fails to register must be counted and skipped, and the run must continue with the remaining subs -- exactly what the framesRejected counter was written for. Losing an entire night's stack to one satellite-trailed or wind-shaken sub is the single most expensive failure mode this feature has. The dialog should end with 'Stacked 6 of 8 subs - 2 rejected (alignment)'.
repro: 1. Imaging > Stack > Stack & Share on an 8-sub session, turn 'Apply calibration' off, press Start. 2. Watch the log: 'Adding frame to stack: .../audit_L_018.fits' then 'Frame rejected: alignment residual 10.34px exceeds max 10.00px (28 matches)' then 'Live stacker stopped'. 3. Dialog reads 'Stack & Share failed'. 4. sqlite3 skotiq.db 'select count(*) from stacked_results' -> unchanged (1, the pre-seeded row); no new row for this run.
evidence: App log 2026-08-02T14:53:10: 'Live stacker initialized: 512x512 reference with 34 stars' / 'Adding frame to stack: audit_L_018.fits' / 'WARN Frame rejected: alignment residual 10.34px exceeds max 10.00px (28 matches)' / 'Live stacker stopped and resources released'. UI: 'Stack & Share failed - SkotiqError.imageError(field0: Alignment residual too high: 10.34px (max 10.00px))'. DB: stacked_results count 1 before and after.
where: packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/services/stack_and_share_service.dart:328 (`final result = await _addStackFrame(...)` inside the followers loop, no try/catch) and the now-unreachable framesRejected accounting at :335-340; run-level catch that deletes the row at :484.
proposed_fix: Wrap the _addStackFrame await in a try/catch that increments framesRejected, records the reason, emits progress and continues; only fail the run if the surviving stacked count is below a floor (e.g. < 2 frames). Surface the rejected count and the most common reason in the completion state.
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced live, twice. With 'Apply calibration' off: 'Live stacker initialized: 512x512 reference with 34 stars' / 'Adding frame to stack: audit_L_017.fits' / 'Frame 2 stacked (2 total, 0 rejected)' / 'Adding frame to stack: audit_L_018.fits' / 'WARN Frame rejected: alignment residual 10.34px exceeds max 10.00px (28 matches)' / 'Live stacker stopped and resources released' 1 ms later. Frames 019-024 never attempted; dialog read 'Stack & Share failed - SkotiqError.imageError(field0: Alignment residual too high: 10.34px (max 10.00px))'; stacked_results unchanged at 3 rows before and after both runs. Cited lines are exact: stack_and_share_service.dart:328 is literally 'final result = await _addStackFrame(' inside 'for (final frame in followers)' with no try/catch, and :335-340 is the framesRejected accounting. That counter is genuinely unreachable: every rejection path in stacking.rs (too few stars :447, too few matches :471, residual too high :495) returns Err, and the only Ok path accumulates and increments the stacked count. Location nit: the finding cites :484 for the run-level catch that deletes the row; in the current file the catch is at :486 and the deleteResult call at :493.

title: Settings search is a raw substring match, so any two-word phrase a user would actually type ('capture folder') returns 'No settings match your search'
what_happened: Search 'capture folder' -> 'No settings match your search.' Search 'folder' alone -> Files & Storage, Autofocus, Image Grading. Search 'disk' -> no match, although the Dashboard's own empty-state text is 'Set a capture directory to track free space' and the status bar says 'No save path'. The matcher only finds a result when the typed string is a literal substring of one indexed phrase, so it cannot AND two words together.
expected: Tokenise the query and AND the terms (NINA, macOS System Settings and Windows Settings all do this). The words the app itself uses elsewhere for this feature — 'capture', 'disk', 'free space', 'save path' — should all reach Files & Storage.
repro: Settings > search box > 'capture folder' (no match); then 'folder' (3 matches); then 'disk' (no match).
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsg2/search-montage.png panel 4 ('capture folder' -> No settings match your search.), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsg2/search-montage2.png ('folder' -> 3 hits, 'disk' -> none).
location_wrong: 'where' is vague; the matcher is packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/settings/settings_catalog.dart:79-88 (SettingsSectionDef.matches), not settings_search_index.g.dart.
proposed_fix: Split the query on whitespace and require every token to match some keyword of the section; add 'capture', 'disk', 'free space', 'save path' as synonyms for files-storage.
verdict_reasoning: matches() is three contains(query) calls on the whole un-tokenised query, so no AND is possible. Emulated over the shipped index: 'capture folder' -> [], 'folder' -> ['files-storage','autofocus','image-grading'] (3 hits, exactly as claimed), 'disk' -> [], 'free space' -> [], 'save path' -> []. Live-confirmed 'capture folder' -> 'No settings match your search.' (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/v2sg/06b-capfolder.png). All three of the app's own words for this feature miss the page that owns it.

title: The Share Card's metadata strip is clipped: it renders 'M51  Integration 00:35:00  Frames 7  Fil…' and the filter is cut off the right edge
what_happened: Stack result > Share Card exports a 512x512 RGB PNG whose bottom caption bar reads 'M51   Integration  00:35:00   Frames  7   Fil' and then hits the right edge mid-word. The caption is laid out at a font size derived from the image HEIGHT (ShareCardSpec.fontScale defaults to ShareCardFontScale.scaleToHeight) with no measurement against the available WIDTH, so any card narrower than the caption needs simply truncates. This is the artefact the feature exists to produce -- the thing a user posts publicly -- and it ships with the text running off the edge.
expected: Either measure the caption and shrink the font / wrap to a second line until it fits the card width, or render the card on a fixed-size canvas (e.g. 1200x1200 or 1200x675) with the image letterboxed, so the caption geometry is independent of the stack's pixel dimensions.
repro: 1. Produce any stack result whose image is 512px wide. 2. Stack result screen > 'Share Card' > save to a .png. 3. Open the PNG and read the bottom strip.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/rsr-sharecard.png (copied to /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsr2-12.png): 512x512, bit depth 8, colour type 2; bottom bar reads 'M51 | Integration 00:35:00 | Frames 7 | Fil'. The result screen and the AstroBin sidecar both carry 'Filter L', so the data is present -- only the rendering truncates.
where: packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/models/imaging/stack_and_share_models.dart:644-676 ShareCardSpec (layout bottomBar, fontScale scaleToHeight); composition in packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/services/stack_share_export_service.dart
location_wrong: The truncating code is packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/services/share_card_renderer.dart:360-447 (_drawBottomBar), not stack_share_export_service.dart (which only forwards at :344); the spec itself is stack_and_share_models.dart:642-676 as cited.
proposed_fix: Add a width-fitting pass: measure the composed caption at the height-derived size and reduce the size (or split into two rows) until it fits within the card width minus padding. Add a regression test that renders a 512-wide card and asserts the caption's measured width is <= card width.
verdict_reasoning: Recomputed the geometry myself rather than trusting the screenshot. I ran the shipped ShareCardRenderer against the exact spec stack_result_screen.dart:852 builds (title 'M51', stats Integration 00:35:00 / Frames 7 / Filter L, targetWidth=targetHeight=result dimensions=512). fontForHeight(512) -> 20.5 -> img.arial24, lineHeight 28, pad 14, gap 11. Summing xAdvance exactly as _drawBottomBar does: 'M51' 14..60, 'Integration  00:35:00' 93..311, 'Frames  7' 344..452, 'Filter  L' starts at 485 and needs 80px -> ends at 565, i.e. 53px past the 512px right edge. Rendering the PNG for real and scanning the caption band shows bright glyph pixels running to column 511, so the last segment is cut mid-word as reported. Nothing measures the caption against the card WIDTH -- the only width logic is `if (x >= bitmap.width - pad) break;` and drawString clips the remainder.

title: Automatic backups are ON by default and write to ~/Documents/Skotiq/backups, a location the Files & Storage page never names and offers no way to change
what_happened: 'Enable automatic backups' defaults ON with a 24 h interval and 'Maximum backups 7'. The page shows File Paths for 'Image output' and 'Sequences' and says application data is 'Managed automatically in Skotiq's application data folder' — but it never says where backups go. They go to getApplicationDocumentsDirectory()/Skotiq/backups, i.e. ~/Documents/Skotiq/backups, which ignores SKOTIQ_DATA_DIR entirely: this sandboxed audit instance, whose data dir is /tmp/ns-audit/r-settings-general/data, wrote its backups into the real user's Documents folder. 'Maximum backups' then PRUNES files in that undisclosed directory.
expected: The Status section should show the backup folder path with a 'Reveal' action and let the user change it (backups belong on the same drive the user actually backs up, and an observatory PC's Documents folder is often the smallest volume). Retention that deletes files must name the folder it deletes from. Honouring the configured data directory is the minimum.
repro: Fresh profile with SKOTIQ_DATA_DIR=/tmp/ns-audit/r-settings-general/data. Wait 5 min or press Back Up Now. `find /tmp/ns-audit/r-settings-general -iname '*backup*'` -> nothing; `ls ~/Documents/Skotiq/backups` -> skotiq_autosave_2026-08-02T10-27-45.572326.nsbackup and two more from this run.
evidence: backup_service.dart:1025-1030 `_getBackupDirectory` = getApplicationDocumentsDirectory()/Skotiq/backups with no settings override wired up; observed files listed above; /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsg2/07-files-scroll.png shows the Status card with no path.
proposed_fix: Add a 'Backup folder' path row to Files & Storage (browse + reveal), default it under the app data dir, and show the resolved path in the Status card.
verdict_reasoning: HALF of this is already fixed and must not be re-fixed. The path half is FIXED: backup_service.dart:1051-1055 _getBackupDirectory now calls the new resolveDefaultBackupDirectory() (:135-145), which resolves 'backups/' beside resolveDefaultDatabaseFile(environment) and therefore honours SKOTIQ_DATABASE_DIR. Verified live: this sandboxed instance wrote /tmp/ns-audit/v2-settings-general/data/backups/skotiq_autosave_2026-08-03T16-44-36.898434.nsbackup, and 'find ~/Documents/Skotiq/backups -newermt 2026-08-03' returns nothing. The disclosure half still reproduces: AutoSaveConfig defaults are backupEnabled=true, backupInterval=24h, maxBackups=7 (auto_save_service.dart:26-33), and the Status section (auto_save_settings.dart:306-372) renders only 'Last backup', 'Last error' and a 'Back Up Now' button — it never names the directory and offers no way to change it, while 'Maximum backups' prunes files in that unnamed folder. Severity dropped to P3 now that the cross-install/undeclared-volume leak is gone.
